rising.description: Open-source, local-first social media research agent for Instagram, TikTok, and LinkedIn. Jev routes read-only steps; socai CLI captures cited browser evidence.

Produces source-cited reports with recorded example output
Open source with a tests badge and a stated release version
risks: Runs through the user's logged-in browser sessions, which raises platform terms and account-safety concerns
Profile and comment extraction could be used to build dossiers on individuals
Heavy reliance on a separate socai CLI and an OpenRouter key

rising.description: An agent skill that finds where a photo was taken — OpenStreetMap geometry, elevation skylines, satellite imagery and street view — and shows its work. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and GitHub Copilot.

strengths: Clear multi-stage pipeline with named scripts and data sources
Shows its work with evidence overlays
Works across several agent platforms with setup instructions
risks: Geolocating photos may be misused to locate private places or people
Depends on Chrome/Chromium and external services for reverse image search

rising.description: 🔎 Username, email & phone OSINT — 9,700+ lookup checks from 19 projects, with profile enrichment, bulk searches, evidence graphs and expert-reviewed updates.
rising.summary: Consensus is a Python CLI and GUI that runs username, email and phone lookups across about 9,700 site modules from 19 open-source projects, with profile enrichment, bulk searches, evidence graphs, PDF reports and an MCP server for AI assistants.
strengths: Large consolidated module set with a stated review process
Windows installer, PyPI package and source install options
Evidence graph and PDF reporting for investigations
risks: Mass username and email lookups can enable profiling of private individuals
Claims of weekly expert review are unverified marketing

rising.description: Scrape Facebook GraphQL data without an API key — profiles, posts, comments, reactions, groups, marketplace, search_engine.

strengths: Documented API with property and method listings for profiles, posts, comments and groups
Auto-recovers changed GraphQL Doc IDs without a headless browser
risks: Uses personal session cookies and likely violates Facebook terms of service
Lead-generation framing suggests bulk collection of personal data
Abandonment risk from reliance on undocumented internal endpoints

rising.description: Wireshark for the radio spectrum: channelize a wide span once, decode every signal in it at once
rising.summary: Desktop SDR tool that channelizes a wide radio band and decodes many signal types at once, including ISM devices, ADS-B, AIS, APRS, pagers, DMR, TETRA, LoRa and radiosondes, with recording and an agent option.
strengths: Decodes many protocols from one wide-band capture
Named decoders and bands with a clear install path
Passive reception of public transmissions
risks: Intercepting TETRA and DMR traffic with decryption and key recovery raises legal concerns
Records voice and messages, which may capture private communications
Agent can transmit on radio, requiring licensing awareness

rising.description: Continuously updated catalogue of open-source OSINT tools, skills, plugins, MCP servers, and agentic integrations.
rising.summary: A continuously updated, hand-reviewed catalogue of open-source OSINT tools, MCP servers, agent skills and agentic integrations, organised by category and by target input, with a CSV database.

Browsable by target input and by category
Provides a CSV database and emerging/agentic subsets
risks: Catalogue quality depends on maintenance; last update timestamp is recent but unverified
Listing tools does not itself vet their legal or ethical use

rising.description: An OSINT investigation case mapping tool for organizing entities, relationships, evidence, and intelligence.
rising.summary: A local, offline investigation case tool for profiling subjects, mapping link networks with shortest path and centrality, placing locations on a map, building timelines, storing evidence with an audit log, and exporting PDF or HTML reports.
strengths: Runs locally with no server or telemetry
Concrete features: link network analysis, timeline, evidence vault with audit log
Install options and sample case reports provided
risks: Subject profiling of individuals could be misused for personal data collection
Limited detail on data sources and legal considerations

rising.description: Free alternative to https://osint-ui.com
rising.summary: A free, browser-based suite of about 20 OSINT tools covering username, email, breach, password-hash, DNS and certificate lookups, with a FastAPI backend for some tools. Positioned as a free alternative to osint-ui.com.
strengths: Many tools with named free public data sources
Browser-first design keeps analysed files local
Explicit passive-only stance and documented data sources
risks: Username and email lookups can support personal-data inference
Licence combines Apache 2.0 with Commons Clause, limiting commercial use
Readme digest is truncated, so some tool details are unverified

rising.description: High-Performance Wayback Machine CDX Recon & Triage Workspace for Chrome (Manifest V3). Stream archived URLs, rank by security risk, verify live 200s, and export.
rising.summary: Chrome Manifest V3 extension that streams Wayback Machine CDX archived URLs, ranks them by security risk (.env, keys, .git, SQL dumps), mines parameters, verifies live 200s, and exports results.
strengths: Concrete features: streaming CDX parsing, risk tiers, live HEAD verification
Runs locally as an unpacked extension with clear install steps
Zero-tracking privacy stance stated
risks: Security-recon framing leans toward attack-surface work with bug-bounty and fuzzing emphasis
Some README claims are marketing-style (High-Performance, Zero Tracking badges)

rising.description: ⚒️ Open-source OSINT and digital forensics skills for AI assistants. Investigate sources, challenge hypotheses, analyze artifacts, and produce evidence-referenced reports with portable case files and offline Python tools. Designed for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and Gemini CLI.
rising.summary: A set of 16 agent skills for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Gemini CLI that turn sources and artifacts into portable case files with preserved evidence, referenced findings, and offline Python tools.

Offline Python runtime with stated limits and no telemetry
Multiple export formats including GraphML and EN/FR reports
risks: Reliance on host assistant for web research and model data transmission
Recorded trials do not establish accuracy gains, per the README

rising.description: A responsible, open-source Instagram username availability scanner. Async CLI with bounded concurrency, rate-limit backoff, resumable scans, Docker and GitHub Actions support.

strengths: Documents clear limitations and that results are not guaranteed claimable
Resumable checkpoints and conservative UNKNOWN classification
Concrete example run and multiple output formats
risks: Brute-force enumeration of platform accounts may conflict with Instagram terms of service
Usefulness for OSINT is limited; mainly a username availability tool
Scope is contestable since the purpose is registration availability rather than investigation

rising.description: AI agent skill that finds a person's accounts across ~450 sites from a plain description, verifies which are really them, and writes an HTML report. Works in Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Copilot, Cursor and OpenCode.
rising.summary: An AI agent skill that turns a person description into username variants, checks them against Sherlock's site list across about 450 sites, verifies matches, and produces a self-contained HTML report.
strengths: Clear install path for multiple agents
Built on the established Sherlock site list
Includes a responsible use section
risks: Targets named individuals' accounts, enabling profiling
README gives limited detail on verification method and data limits
Primarily an agent wrapper around an existing tool

rising.description: 🎯 The ultimate OSINT toolkit: investigation graph, confidence scoring, alias families, map, timeline and reports. 49 modules, 400+ sites, no API keys required.
rising.summary: Desktop OSINT platform that starts from a username, email, phone, name, domain, IP or Chilean RUT and builds an investigation graph with confidence scoring, alias detection, a map, a timeline and reports across 49 modules.

Works without API keys and runs locally
Chilean-specific sources such as RUT lookup

Chilean RUT lookup may touch national-ID data
README marketing claims exceed the detail shown

rising.description: Track the flights that carry weapons. Free, open-source flight search, live map and AI research assistant for journalists. In memory of Sha'ban al-Dalou.
rising.summary: SADA is a free open-source tool that searches a multi-year ADS-B flight archive, with an AI assistant, live map and documented weapons-shipment cases, to help journalists trace flights carrying arms.

Explicit guidance on reading observed versus inferred flights and on what the data cannot show

Reliance on paid OpenRouter or Anthropic keys for the assistant

rising.description: Instagram Scraper — free, open-source Instagram scraper. Unlimited profiles, posts, reels, comments and hashtags as clean JSON, no API key, no proxies.
rising.summary: A Python API that scrapes public Instagram profiles, posts, reels, comments and hashtags into JSON, run locally via a FastAPI-style server with 19 endpoints. Marketed as free and unlimited.
strengths: Runnable local API with a curl example
Clear endpoint coverage for profiles, posts, comments and hashtags
Open-source and installable from requirements
risks: Scrapes personal profile data and email addresses, raising privacy concerns
Marketing claims of unlimited data without stated limits or legal considerations
Likely to break against Instagram changes; bundled promotional content

rising.description: Self-scan CLI that shows what an attacker can build from your own public data. Keyless, read-only, local-first.

Documents its collectors, public sources and read-only design in a clear table
Local-first with no API keys or cloud dependency

Person-level lookup tool that could be pointed at others despite the self-scan framing

rising.description: GeoWeb — find where any photo (or video) was taken. A local-first, open-source browser console around the GeoInt recon pipeline, with Docker, docs and a GitHub Pages landing site.

Shows evidence and caveats so the analyst makes the final call
Documented quickstart, Docker setup and demo sessions

Young project with limited history evident from the digest

Installable via pip, cargo, or prebuilt binaries with documented inputs and outputs
risks: Depends on a free Frost API key and external data service
Accuracy limits depend on recording and data quality; findings should be treated as probabilistic

Emphasises passive-first methodology and sourced, confidence-rated findings
Includes install script and reference cookbooks

Covers profile extraction, username enumeration and reporting in one tool

Every reading traceable to its publisher

geospatial-imagery.description: PictoSINT — An image-focused OSINT and intelligence toolkit for metadata analysis, visual investigation, geolocation research, and digital forensics.
geospatial-imagery.summary: PICTOSINT analyses photographs for geolocation clues. It combines CLIP landmark recognition, OCR, Nominatim geocoding and satellite imagery to generate and verify location hypotheses, with HTML and JSON reports.
strengths: Combines visual, OCR and geocoding signals into candidate locations
Verifies hypotheses against satellite imagery
Outputs HTML and JSON reports
risks: Documentation is high level with few usage examples
Limited detail on setup or data source limits

identity-lookup.description: 🔎 Username, email & phone OSINT — 9,700+ lookup checks from 19 projects, with profile enrichment, bulk searches, evidence graphs and expert-reviewed updates.
identity-lookup.summary: Consensus is a Python CLI and GUI that runs username, email and phone lookups across about 9,700 site modules from 19 open-source projects, with profile enrichment, bulk searches, evidence graphs, PDF reports and an MCP server for AI assistants.
strengths: Large consolidated module set with a stated review process
Windows installer, PyPI package and source install options
Evidence graph and PDF reporting for investigations
risks: Mass username and email lookups can enable profiling of private individuals
Claims of weekly expert review are unverified marketing

identity-lookup.description: Self-scan CLI that shows what an attacker can build from your own public data. Keyless, read-only, local-first.
identity-lookup.summary: A keyless, read-only CLI that verifies ownership of an email address, then gathers public traces (accounts, leaks, photo GPS, git identity) about you and builds a local profile and report. An optional mode generates a simulated phishing email and a non-submitting login page.
strengths: Ownership verification is enforced in code before any scan
Documents its collectors, public sources and read-only design in a clear table
Local-first with no API keys or cloud dependency
risks: Optional --attack mode generates personalized phishing email content, which could be repurposed
Person-level lookup tool that could be pointed at others despite the self-scan framing
Relies on an optional local LLM for profiling, so output quality and behaviour are not fully specified

identity-lookup.description: A responsible, open-source Instagram username availability scanner. Async CLI with bounded concurrency, rate-limit backoff, resumable scans, Docker and GitHub Actions support.
identity-lookup.summary: Async Python CLI that generates short Instagram usernames and checks public profile pages to flag names with no visible profile. Supports rate-limit backoff, resumable scans, and txt, json, or csv output. Results are candidates only and must be verified on Instagram.
strengths: Documents clear limitations and that results are not guaranteed claimable
Resumable checkpoints and conservative UNKNOWN classification
Concrete example run and multiple output formats
risks: Brute-force enumeration of platform accounts may conflict with Instagram terms of service
Usefulness for OSINT is limited; mainly a username availability tool
Scope is contestable since the purpose is registration availability rather than investigation

identity-lookup.description: AI agent skill that finds a person's accounts across ~450 sites from a plain description, verifies which are really them, and writes an HTML report. Works in Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Copilot, Cursor and OpenCode.
identity-lookup.summary: An AI agent skill that turns a person description into username variants, checks them against Sherlock's site list across about 450 sites, verifies matches, and produces a self-contained HTML report.
strengths: Clear install path for multiple agents
Built on the established Sherlock site list
Includes a responsible use section
risks: Targets named individuals' accounts, enabling profiling
README gives limited detail on verification method and data limits
Primarily an agent wrapper around an existing tool

identity-lookup.description: Async, plugin-based OSINT recon for usernames, emails & names — 90+ sources, confidence-scored, built for Kali Linux
identity-lookup.summary: Async, plugin-based Python CLI that fans out username, email, phone and name queries across dozens of platforms and APIs, scores result confidence, correlates identities, and exports terminal, JSON, CSV, HTML or graph reports.
strengths: Clear confidence labelling separating confirmed from probable hits
Documented sources and config setup check
Offline phone number parsing
risks: Person-level lookup across breach and identity sources raises privacy concerns
Relies on many third-party APIs and enumeration sites that may change
Usage legal considerations not clearly documented in the excerpt

identity-lookup.description: Cross-platform OSINT reconnaissance: 65 social/dev/media vectors, avatar clustering, DNS/PGP enrichment, dossier export via CLI & web UI.
identity-lookup.summary: Local-first Node.js reconnaissance tool that takes a username, email or domain, probes 65 public platforms, runs DNS, PGP and avatar-hash enrichment, and exports a correlated identity dossier via CLI or web UI.
strengths: Zero npm dependencies and zero-account probes
Documents probe strategies and enrichment pipeline
Clear ethical use section
risks: Person-focused identity correlation could enable profiling of individuals
Initial v1.0.0 release with limited track record
Author self-describes project quality with marketing-style claims

identity-lookup.description: TikTok User Info Scraper & Username Reconnaissance Framework - A strategic OSINT & cybersecurity reconnaissance tool for TikTok profile intelligence gathering, cross-platform username enumeration, and digital footprint analysis.
identity-lookup.summary: A pure Bash terminal tool that scrapes public TikTok profile data, enumerates a username across 75+ platforms, checks Wayback Machine snapshots and TLS/DNS details, and generates search dorks and TSV/JSONL reports.
strengths: Runs on Termux, Linux and macOS with minimal dependencies
Covers profile extraction, username enumeration and reporting in one tool
risks: Scraping TikTok profiles and enumerating usernames can enable tracking of individuals
Marketing-heavy README with hacking-oriented topics and tags like tiktok-bot-reporters suggest possible abuse
Thin usage detail and no clear legal or rate-limit considerations beyond a disclaimer

identity-lookup.description: Local async OSINT with public sources, evidence-backed relationship graphs, offline reports and a Python API. No API keys.
identity-lookup.summary: Atlas is a local async OSINT tool that starts from a username, email or phone number, queries 76 public username sources and other checks, and builds evidence-backed relationship graphs with offline reports and a Python API. No API keys needed.
strengths: Evidence provenance and explicit warning that a username match is not proof of identity
Local-first with offline demo and API/SDK
risks: Username search across many sites enables profile aggregation about individuals
Interface currently Russian-only documentation partly; Beta release

identity-lookup.description: Recherche et corrélation de pseudonymes sur ~3200 sites, avec score explicable et graphe de relations. Autohébergé, sources publiques uniquement.
identity-lookup.summary: Self-hosted web app that searches a username across about 3200 sites, correlates found accounts to one person, enriches via public APIs, and shows results as a relationship graph with an explainable score. Includes legal framing and per-search logging.
strengths: Explainable scoring and relationship graph
Self-hosted with Docker Compose setup
Documents legal framework and limits
risks: Targets personal data of third parties without consent; misuse for stalking possible
Correlation may produce false identity links (homonymy acknowledged)
Built on maigret-style username enumeration

identity-lookup.description: Check simultaneously if a phone number is registered on popular apps & websites, without any prerequisite 📞
identity-lookup.summary: Go CLI and TUI that checks in parallel whether a phone number is registered on several popular apps and websites. Offers JSON output, privacy-conscious logging, and a single-target scope.
strengths: Concrete CLI usage with parallel module checks and JSON output
Privacy-conscious logging and silent-by-default modules
Cross-platform binaries and go install path
risks: Phone-number registration checks can enable targeting of private individuals
Installation section is partly unfinished (work-in-progress notes)
Legal section relies on a non-OSI internal-use license

knowledge.description: Continuously updated catalogue of open-source OSINT tools, skills, plugins, MCP servers, and agentic integrations.
knowledge.summary: A continuously updated, hand-reviewed catalogue of open-source OSINT tools, MCP servers, agent skills and agentic integrations, organised by category and by target input, with a CSV database.
strengths: Large, categorised catalogue of roughly 495 projects
Browsable by target input and by category
Provides a CSV database and emerging/agentic subsets
risks: Catalogue quality depends on maintenance; last update timestamp is recent but unverified
Listing tools does not itself vet their legal or ethical use

knowledge.description: In late September and early October of 2026 numerous Japanese organizations reported breaches and data leaks. This repository keeps track of such reports.
knowledge.summary: A curated, date-ordered list of reported data breaches and leaks at Japanese organisations, with company profiles, impact notes and source links to news articles and official notices.
strengths: Organised by date with sourced reports
Notes uncertainty in reported leaks
risks: Relies on translated and secondary reporting
Contains unverified claims about leaked data
Repository has no detailed methodology

knowledge.description: ADINT: a field guide to ad-tech surveillance. How advertising data (MAID, RTB bidstream, SDK location) becomes warrantless intelligence.
knowledge.summary: A field guide documenting how advertising data such as mobile ad IDs, RTB bidstream and SDK location feeds is used for surveillance. It catalogues data brokers, vendors, government buyers, regulators, timelines and sources, with RSS feeds.
strengths: Structured roster of entities, glossary and timeline with cited public sources
Maintained sources list with RSS feeds for monitoring
risks: Content is a research compilation rather than a tool; limited executable functionality

knowledge.description: Country-by-country dossiers on the global surveillance industry, spyware vendors, state agencies and Palantir.
knowledge.summary: A Markdown research repository of country-by-country dossiers on the global surveillance industry, covering spyware vendors, state agencies, data brokers and Palantir. The README digest shows structure and badges but few concrete sources or methods.
strengths: Organised as per-country dossiers with a clear topic scope
Covers vendors, state agencies and data brokers in one place
risks: Coverage section is empty in the README digest
Digest shows little on sourcing or verification methodology

media-forensics.description: Trace file provenance, metadata, telemetry, investigative pivots and relationships across files, browser history, OS traces and archives. Local, read-only, no network requests.
media-forensics.summary: Local, read-only CLI that examines files for provenance, embedded metadata, C2PA, browser and OS traces, and investigative identifiers, correlating findings into an evidence graph with exports.
strengths: Local and read-only with no network requests during analysis
Clear evidence sources and supported formats documented
Corroboration and conflict tracking with source attribution
risks: Pivot extraction can surface personal identifiers such as accounts, financial and geographic data
Feature-heavy README; real-world maturity not independently verified

media-forensics.description: Local-first digital image forensics & pixel analysis workbench with 44 registered inspection modules.
media-forensics.summary: A local-first Flask web app that runs 44 pixel and metadata forensics modules on a single uploaded image, including bit-plane, ELA and anomaly views, and exports self-contained HTML and PDF reports.
strengths: Runs locally with clear setup steps for Windows, macOS and Linux
Many named analysis modules with HTML and PDF report export
Explicitly frames results as analyst aids rather than authenticity verdicts
risks: Tangential to OSINT; primarily general image forensics
Some README content is UI and theme detail rather than analytical methodology

media-forensics.description: Detect hidden, residual, and machine-readable content in documents, images, and files.
media-forensics.summary: Python CLI that scans PDFs, spreadsheets, presentations, images and other files for hidden, covered or residual content and failed redactions, reporting mismatches between what a human sees and what a parser extracts. Outputs text, JSON, Markdown or HTML reports.
strengths: Local, read-only, no network requests
Detailed detector reference and clear evidence model
Installable via PyPI with minimal dependencies
risks: Overlaps with general document forensics rather than investigating people directly
Limited external validation visible in the digest

media-forensics.description: Open-source, cross-platform document discovery & metadata reconnaissance tool  a modern, Windows-free alternative to FOCA.
media-forensics.summary: Python CLI and local web UI that discovers PDF and Office documents on target domains via crawling, sitemaps, Wayback Machine and search dorking, then extracts metadata with ExifTool to report leaked usernames and other data.
strengths: Clear FOCA-style purpose with named sources and tools
Cross-platform install instructions for macOS, Linux and Windows
Documented CLI, web UI, REST API and Docker options
risks: Can expose authors and internal usernames of target organisations, a potential misuse vector
Optional PII content scanning and sensitive-file discovery broaden scope

media-forensics.description: A tri-branch digital media forensics workstation for detecting AI-generated synthetic images (Diffusion/GANs) and Photoshop tampering with calibrated Conformal Prediction guarantees.
media-forensics.summary: A Flask-based workstation that analyses uploaded images for AI-generated content and Photoshop tampering. It computes hashes, reads EXIF and C2PA provenance, runs FFT, NPR and ELA checks, and produces a multi-page PDF forensic dossier with conformal confidence sets.
strengths: Named methods and standards with concrete outputs such as hashes, heatmaps and a PDF dossier
Includes Docker deployment, a test suite and benchmark scripts
risks: Accuracy and court-defensibility claims are not backed by independent validation in the README excerpt
Detection of AI images is an arms race, so results may be unreliable on new generators

media-forensics.description: LocBITE - Location, Binary, Image, Temporal, EXIF... is a professional photo forensics and metadata extraction tool for cybersecurity professionals, digital forensic investigators, OSINT analysts, and researchers. It extracts hidden image intelligence including GPS location, EXIF data, timestamps, device information etc
media-forensics.summary: Python CLI for photo forensics that extracts EXIF metadata, GPS location, timestamps, device info, steganographic content and OCR text from images, with a WhatsApp media scanning option and report export.
strengths: Clear forensic use cases including evidence validation
Lists dependencies and install steps for desktop and Termux
risks: Marketing-heavy README with little detail on outputs or limits
Counter-terrorism and cybercrime framing with no legal or consent guidance
Includes WhatsApp directory and database scanning, which may touch private data

media-forensics.description: Análisis de metadatos EXIF del reto BreadCrumbs (OSINT · The Breach · ThePwnLab, plataforma del Bootcamp de Ciberseguridad de The Bridge): reconstrucción con ExifTool de dónde y cuándo se tomaron cinco fotografías a partir de sus coordenadas GPS y marcas de tiempo.
media-forensics.summary: A CTF writeup showing how to use ExifTool to extract capture dates and GPS coordinates from five photos and reconstruct a route, with notes on metadata reliability. Written in Spanish.
strengths: Clear step-by-step ExifTool commands
Explains metadata reliability and manual editing caveat
risks: Narrow CTF writeup rather than a reusable tool
Ships no code; only a walkthrough of a single challenge

situational-awareness.description: Wireshark for the radio spectrum: channelize a wide span once, decode every signal in it at once
situational-awareness.summary: Desktop SDR tool that channelizes a wide radio band and decodes many signal types at once, including ISM devices, ADS-B, AIS, APRS, pagers, DMR, TETRA, LoRa and radiosondes, with recording and an agent option.
strengths: Decodes many protocols from one wide-band capture
Named decoders and bands with a clear install path
Passive reception of public transmissions
risks: Intercepting TETRA and DMR traffic with decryption and key recovery raises legal concerns
Records voice and messages, which may capture private communications
Agent can transmit on radio, requiring licensing awareness

situational-awareness.description: Real-time situational-awareness dashboard for Hong Kong - one map, many official open data sources, no API keys in the client. Open source (AGPL-3.0); not a government system.
situational-awareness.summary: Browser-based live map dashboard consolidating Hong Kong government and institutional open data (traffic cameras, weather, transport, border waits, aircraft positions, markets) with each reading linked to its publisher. Static app with a whitelisted Cloudflare Worker proxy.
strengths: Clear source catalogue with endpoints, cadence and licence in SOURCES.md
Every reading traceable to its publisher
No API keys in client bundle
risks: Mostly a civic dashboard; OSINT framing is light
Proxy routes third-party data, so upstream terms must be respected

situational-awareness.description: Sala de situación abierta de Venezuela: cada cifra con su fuente y su hora. Dólar, internet por estado, censura, sismos, clima, noticias y más, desde fuentes públicas.
situational-awareness.summary: Open, self-hosted situation room for Venezuela aggregating public data on the dollar rate, internet and power outages by state, censorship measurements, earthquakes, weather, airspace notices, live TV and news, each figure with its source and age.
strengths: Every figure is attributed to a source, licence and timestamp
Runs with no keys or accounts; sources catalogued in docs
risks: Aggregates from many third-party sources whose reliability varies
Licence is PolyForm Noncommercial, limiting commercial reuse

situational-awareness.description: OmniScope Web - 100% Serverless Static Geospatial Intelligence & Doppler Weather Radar Dashboard for Cloudflare Pages. Zero cloud database fees, zero server costs, pure open data.
situational-awareness.summary: Serverless static dashboard for Cloudflare Pages that displays open geospatial data such as Doppler weather radar, ISS tracking, earthquakes and webcams, with an MCP server and keyless edge APIs.
strengths: Uses open, keyless public data feeds
Deployable on Cloudflare Pages with documented steps
Includes MCP server and API access
risks: Heavy promotional and trademark-enforcement language with unverifiable claims like certified 147-model consensus
Mostly weather and space monitoring rather than investigative OSINT
Clone-warning wording may signal marketing over substance

situational-awareness.description: Real-time tactical OSINT & GEOINT dashboard. Live flight tracking (ADS-B), maritime vessels, satellites, undersea telecom cables & HUD shaders powered by free, keyless open APIs.
situational-awareness.summary: Open-source tactical dashboard showing live ADS-B aircraft, AIS vessels, satellites, public traffic cameras, earthquakes, and undersea cables on 2D and 3D maps, using free keyless APIs.
strengths: Named public data sources with endpoints listed
Keyless, runnable locally with clear quick-start steps
Explicit disclaimer and honest labelling of non-live data
risks: Marketing-heavy README with some unsupported superlatives
Limited detail on legal considerations for camera feed aggregation

situational-awareness.description: Index of every God's Eye / World Monitor style live world-map intel dashboard on GitHub, with live stars and the feeds they share
situational-awareness.summary: A generated index listing three God's Eye / World Monitor style live world-map intel dashboards on GitHub, with star counts and a catalogue of 26 shared upstream feeds, 17 of them keyless.
strengths: Clear curated scope on live OSINT world-map dashboards
Lists upstream data feeds and their key requirements
Refreshed from a stated data source
risks: Headline star totals and trending claims are not verified in the data
Index covers only three projects, so coverage is thin
Badges and visitor counters add little substance

situational-awareness.description: Karnak — a live OSINT situational monitor: a wall of live streams, an AI situation brief, a fused news timeline, market indicators, and a network-reachability watch. Named for Ozymandias's monitor wall in Watchmen.
situational-awareness.summary: Pantau (codename Karnak) is a single-page dashboard monitoring civic events via public sources: YouTube live streams, an LLM situation brief, a merged news timeline, city activity map, market indicators, volcano alerts, and platform reachability checks. Configurable by country an
strengths: Clear setup with Docker Compose and optional API keys
Configurable sources and keywords for any country or event
States no login and no visitor tracking
risks: Reachability probing from residential connections may raise operational concerns
Political protest monitoring could be misused for surveillance of activists
Some features depend on third-party keys and services

situational-awareness.description: Raion-level air-raid alert onset prediction for Ukraine (15/30/60 min horizons, LightGBM over alert history + OSINT Telegram signals) with a cinematic replay map — KSE Agentic AI School project
situational-awareness.summary: Research prototype predicting which Ukrainian raions will enter air-raid alert within 15/30/60 minutes using LightGBM over alert history and Telegram OSINT signals, with a deck.gl/MapLibre replay map of past attack nights.
strengths: Reproducible pipeline with stated inputs and commands
Honest limitations and negative results documented
Interactive replay map with ground truth comparison
risks: Predictions explicitly not a warning system; misuse risk if treated as alerts
Depends on external non-redistributable Telegram exports
Research prototype with no ongoing maintenance signals

situational-awareness.description: Australia Dashboard is a locally hosted OSINT and geospatial intelligence platform covering Australia, New Zealand and the Pacific region. It features 15 intelligence categories, 101 sourced strategic sites, naval and air bases, AUKUS infrastructure, space ranges, nuclear research, LNG facilities and maritime chokepoints.
situational-awareness.summary: A locally hosted dashboard covering Australia, New Zealand and the Pacific, mapping 101 sourced strategic sites, bases, maritime chokepoints and energy infrastructure, with configurable news feeds classified into 15 intelligence categories.
strengths: Sourced strategic sites with status and date fields
Runs locally with documented launch steps
Clear coverage of geographic scope and categories
risks: External news retrieval was untested in the build
22 of 101 sites are unverified
Public strategic-site mapping of military facilities may raise sensitivity concerns

situational-awareness.description: Myanmar Dashboard is a locally hosted OSINT and geospatial monitoring platform featuring detailed Myanmar maps, state and regional boundaries, airports, air bases, seaports, conflict references, pipelines, regional news, RSS feeds, public Telegram channels, dark-web onion RSS, ransomware intelligence, earthquake data and 15 intelligence categories.
situational-awareness.summary: A locally hosted dashboard that maps Myanmar with boundaries, airports, air bases, seaports, pipelines and conflict references, and aggregates regional news, GDELT, RSS, public Telegram, dark-web RSS, ransomware leak-site claims and USGS earthquake data.
strengths: Clear multi-source OSINT scope with named feeds
Documents a concrete local install and launch path
Honest limitations section noting unverified feeds and approximate markers
risks: Live news retrieval reported as not verified
Dark-web RSS requires Tor, adding operational complexity
Defence-related location mapping could be misused if markers are inaccurate

social-media.description: Open-source, local-first social media research agent for Instagram, TikTok, and LinkedIn. Jev routes read-only steps; socai CLI captures cited browser evidence.
social-media.summary: Local-first research agent that uses an LLM to choose read-only steps, such as searching, opening posts or profiles and reading comments on Instagram, TikTok and LinkedIn. The socai CLI runs them in the user's signed-in Chrome and returns cited evidence for reports.
strengths: Local-first design with read-only operations and documented data flow
Produces source-cited reports with recorded example output
Open source with a tests badge and a stated release version
risks: Runs through the user's logged-in browser sessions, which raises platform terms and account-safety concerns
Profile and comment extraction could be used to build dossiers on individuals
Heavy reliance on a separate socai CLI and an OpenRouter key

social-media.description: Scrape Facebook GraphQL data without an API key — profiles, posts, comments, reactions, groups, marketplace, search_engine.
social-media.summary: Python library that scrapes Facebook's internal GraphQL endpoints using session cookies to extract profiles, posts, comments, reactions, groups and marketplace listings, with auto-rediscovery of Doc IDs via PyMiniRacer.
strengths: Documented API with property and method listings for profiles, posts, comments and groups
Auto-recovers changed GraphQL Doc IDs without a headless browser
risks: Uses personal session cookies and likely violates Facebook terms of service
Lead-generation framing suggests bulk collection of personal data
Abandonment risk from reliance on undocumented internal endpoints

social-media.description: 从 B站海量视频里为一个议题取数：双轴信源评级（A–F × 1–4）、冲突单列、三类缺口声明、检索协议可复现。MCP server + 方法论 skill。
social-media.summary: An MCP server plus methodology skill that gathers public Bilibili videos and comments for a topic, grades sources on a dual axis, lists conflicts, declares evidence gaps, and produces replayable reports with deep and brief modes.
strengths: Dual-axis source grading with conflicts and gaps declared explicitly
Replayable retrieval protocol and bias notes
Real sample report and 14 documented tools
risks: Depends on Bilibili data access that may break or violate platform terms
Scraping of comments may raise platform compliance questions
Documentation is primarily in Chinese with limited legal discussion

social-media.description: Instagram Scraper — free, open-source Instagram scraper. Unlimited profiles, posts, reels, comments and hashtags as clean JSON, no API key, no proxies.
social-media.summary: A Python API that scrapes public Instagram profiles, posts, reels, comments and hashtags into JSON, run locally via a FastAPI-style server with 19 endpoints. Marketed as free and unlimited.
strengths: Runnable local API with a curl example
Clear endpoint coverage for profiles, posts, comments and hashtags
Open-source and installable from requirements
risks: Scrapes personal profile data and email addresses, raising privacy concerns
Marketing claims of unlimited data without stated limits or legal considerations
Likely to break against Instagram changes; bundled promotional content

social-media.summary: Rust CLI and HTTP service that inspects public GitHub profiles, repositories, commit identities and SSH keys, producing JSON, Markdown, text, SVG or PDF reports with source references and caveats about inferred data.
strengths: Clear documented modes (FAST and DEEP) and output formats
Privacy and limitations section and explicit distinction of observed vs inferred data
Does not execute code from inspected repositories
risks: Aggregates personal commit email addresses and activity timezone inferences about individuals
Optional GitLeak enrichment touches leaked-data sources

social-media.description: Who's being heard, not just who's talking. Public social posts of candidates in the 2026 Czech municipal elections across ten cities, collected with Apify into a DuckDB evidence graph and mapped in a static app.
social-media.summary: Starwatch maps public social media posts of 2026 Czech municipal election candidates across ten cities, collected via Apify into a DuckDB graph and shown in a static map app with engagement snapshots.
strengths: Clear methodology: independent ownership verification before attribution
Links every post back to its original source
Explicitly avoids polls and forecasts per Czech pre-election law
risks: Profiles public candidate social accounts, a caution-level person-tracking style of collection
Hackathon-origin project with a fixed snapshot rather than ongoing maintenance

social-media.description: Claude Code skill that reads public Telegram: channels without an account, groups with yours
social-media.summary: Claude Code skill that reads public Telegram channels without an account via t.me/s pages, with search and full history, and reads groups using the user's own account. Returns structured posts with permalinks and dates.
strengths: Works on public channels with no credentials
Structured output with permalinks and dates for verification
Documented demo and stated limits
risks: Group reading requires a personal Telegram account, raising account-safety and terms-of-service concerns
Scraping public pages may conflict with platform terms

social-media.description: 🔮 Early access to the latest ASIMOV Alpha builds for agentic social media intelligence.
social-media.summary: Early-access alpha of ASIMOV, an agent skill that aims to map social graphs across LinkedIn, X, Instagram, Luma and GitHub, enriched with local CRM contact data such as Attio. Distributed as prebuilt binaries.
strengths: Clear social-media intelligence focus with named platforms
Installs as a skill into common personal agents
risks: Scraping social platforms may breach terms of service and privacy law
Enriches public data with confidential contacts, raising personal data concerns
README is thin on methods, limits and legal considerations; closed alpha binaries

social-media.description: Export the complete follower list of any public X (Twitter) account to CSV + JSONL.
social-media.summary: Python CLI that uses a user's session cookies to call X's internal GraphQL API and export the full follower list of a public account to CSV and JSONL, with resume checkpoints and multi-session rotation.
strengths: Concrete usage examples and documented output files
Documents rate limits and resume checkpoint behaviour
Clear flags and maintenance notes for rotating queryIds
risks: Uses session cookies and README admits likely violation of X Terms of Service
Relies on undocumented internal API that may break
Bulk harvesting of follower profiles raises privacy concerns

social-media.description: High-end Telegram OSINT Toolkit built with Telethon. Bulk keyword search, chat export, member enumeration, proxy/Tor support & SQLite. For cybersecurity & intelligence work.
social-media.summary: A Python CLI built on Telethon for keyword search across Telegram channels, chat and media export, member enumeration, user/channel profiling, live monitoring and SQLite storage, with proxy and Tor support.
strengths: Concrete CLI commands with example inputs and outputs
Multiple export formats and persistent SQLite storage
Includes legal and ethical notice and rate-limit awareness
risks: Member enumeration and user profiling can target private individuals
Marketing-heavy README claims such as 'High-end' and 'Production Ready' without evidence
Requires personal Telegram API credentials; no independent testing evident

transport-sensor.description: Track the flights that carry weapons. Free, open-source flight search, live map and AI research assistant for journalists. In memory of Sha'ban al-Dalou.
transport-sensor.summary: SADA is a free open-source tool that searches a multi-year ADS-B flight archive, with an AI assistant, live map and documented weapons-shipment cases, to help journalists trace flights carrying arms.
strengths: Clear data sources (ADSB.lol archive, Cloudflare R2) and stated limits of coverage
Explicit guidance on reading observed versus inferred flights and on what the data cannot show
risks: Flight-tracking of state arms transfers could be contested politically; findings need careful verification
Reliance on paid OpenRouter or Anthropic keys for the assistant

transport-sensor.description: Android Wi-Fi/BLE radar terminal with camera-maker, tracker, Flock and public safety signatures. Works alone or with an optional CYD over USB.
transport-sensor.summary: Android app that scans nearby Wi-Fi and Bluetooth signals, showing signal strength and matching manufacturer signatures for cameras, trackers, and public safety devices such as Flock Safety and Axon. Optionally pairs with an ESP32-based CYD board over USB for extra radio readings
strengths: Documents limits and false-positive caveats clearly
Published signed APK and firmware with verification docs
risks: Tracker and camera signatures could be used to locate individuals
Ethical framing centred on surveillance of law enforcement equipment

transport-sensor.description: God's Eye View 中文版 — 浏览器里的开源空间情报三维地球，附运行时中文界面外挂与 macOS 双击启动器。Chinese localization of bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view.
transport-sensor.summary: A browser-based 3D globe that combines public live feeds (aircraft, ships, satellites, earthquakes, traffic, public cameras) with a voice agent. This entry is a Chinese localization of the upstream project.
strengths: Aggregates many public sensor feeds on one globe
Runs locally with inspectable source and no required API keys
risks: Localization fork of an upstream project; content largely mirrors original
CCTV poses and launch trajectories are described as coarse estimates

web-capture.description: High-Performance Wayback Machine CDX Recon & Triage Workspace for Chrome (Manifest V3). Stream archived URLs, rank by security risk, verify live 200s, and export.
web-capture.summary: Chrome Manifest V3 extension that streams Wayback Machine CDX archived URLs, ranks them by security risk (.env, keys, .git, SQL dumps), mines parameters, verifies live 200s, and exports results.
strengths: Concrete features: streaming CDX parsing, risk tiers, live HEAD verification
Runs locally as an unpacked extension with clear install steps
Zero-tracking privacy stance stated
risks: Security-recon framing leans toward attack-surface work with bug-bounty and fuzzing emphasis
Some README claims are marketing-style (High-Performance, Zero Tracking badges)

web-capture.description: Proof of what a web page said, and when. Independent witnesses sign and timestamp captures; anyone can verify them offline.
web-capture.summary: Keepword is a decentralized network of independent witnesses that fetch, sign and timestamp web page captures (using drand and Bitcoin) so anyone can later verify what a page said and when, offline.
strengths: Cryptographic sealing and independent witnesses make captures verifiable
Clear install instructions with a labelled release and CI
risks: Network described as early days; limited adoption so far
Relies on a self-hosted node network, so availability depends on witnesses

web-capture.description: Offline OSINT triage for saved HTML: link inventories, host summaries, line references and SHA-256 evidence hashes. Zero runtime dependencies.
web-capture.summary: Lucerna is an offline CLI that inventories HTTP(S) references in saved HTML pages, groups destination hosts, records line numbers, hashes the original file with SHA-256, and compares two saved reports to show changes. It makes no network requests.
strengths: Works fully offline with zero runtime dependencies
Hashes inputs and records provenance for evidence handling
Concrete CLI examples and JSON/CSV/Markdown outputs
risks: Early-stage project with limited community signals
Narrow scope: extracts links rather than broader investigation features

web-capture.description: Ferramenta de dorking em múltiplos motores de busca para coleta de URLs em operações de OSINT e reconhecimento.
web-capture.summary: SimpleReconDorking runs search dorks in parallel across multiple search engines and returns the union of found URLs. Supports dork strings, files, a built-in categorised catalogue, and stdin, with Docker install and usage examples.
strengths: Clear purpose and multiple input modes
Documented usage examples and Docker setup
Built-in dork catalogue by category
risks: Dorking can be used to find exposed targets; README carries a consent warning only
Some engines require browser bypass, which may violate terms of service

web-capture.summary: Python client that queries a CIRCL-hosted Common Crawl index service to search archived web pages by URL, hostname, FQDN or digest, and retrieves only the selected WARC byte ranges. Access requires a token issued by CIRCL on request.
strengths: Queries metadata index before fetching, avoiding full crawl downloads
Documents multiple search modes and output formats with examples
risks: Depends on a token-gated third-party service with discretionary access
Access controls and README sample commands are partially truncated

web-capture.description: Ferramenta de extração e descoberta de URLs para fluxos de OSINT e reconhecimento
web-capture.summary: Python CLI that takes seed URLs, fetches pages and passive/active sources to extract and discover reachable URLs, with optional same-origin spidering, recursive rounds, Docker support and API-key-based sources.
strengths: Clear purpose for URL discovery in recon workflows
Supports passive and active sources, crawling and Docker
Documents usage flags, profiles and presets
risks: Active probing of target sites may raise authorisation concerns
Readme digest shows template-like source examples, limited detail on data sources

web-capture.description: GOBLIN TSUNAMI - OSINT framework generating 400+ Google Dorks across Instagram, Threads, Facebook & TikTok. Advanced digital footprint analysis with 25+ tracking categories for cybersecurity professionals, threat intelligence, and ethical reconnaissance operations.
web-capture.summary: Python framework that generates large sets of Google dork queries targeting Instagram, Threads, Facebook and TikTok to map an individual's digital footprint across tracking categories. README is mostly marketing with little concrete usage detail.
strengths: Clear dork-generation purpose across four platforms
Install instructions provided
risks: Targets individuals' digital footprints, enabling person tracking and location profiling
Heavy marketing language with few concrete examples or limits
Placeholder links and repository URLs suggest unfinished project

workspace-analysis.description: An OSINT investigation case mapping tool for organizing entities, relationships, evidence, and intelligence.
workspace-analysis.summary: A local, offline investigation case tool for profiling subjects, mapping link networks with shortest path and centrality, placing locations on a map, building timelines, storing evidence with an audit log, and exporting PDF or HTML reports.
strengths: Runs locally with no server or telemetry
Concrete features: link network analysis, timeline, evidence vault with audit log
Install options and sample case reports provided
risks: Subject profiling of individuals could be misused for personal data collection
Limited detail on data sources and legal considerations

workspace-analysis.description: Collaborative peer-to-peer OSINT investigation board — end-to-end encrypted, no server-side data, works offline. Desktop app for Windows & Linux.
workspace-analysis.summary: COSINT is an offline-capable, peer-to-peer desktop investigation board for Windows and Linux. Analysts map entities, link them, grade sources, and collaborate in real time with end-to-end encryption and no server-side storage.
strengths: Clear architecture with E2E encrypted P2P sync and no backend
Concrete features: entity taxonomy, Admiralty source grading, .trace export
Multilingual UI and offline and 100% local modes
risks: Mostly case-management tooling rather than data collection
Tests and badges are self-reported; no independent verification of claims

workspace-analysis.description: Watchdog (branding subject to change) is an open-source intelligence (OSINT) case management platform for small teams.
workspace-analysis.summary: Open-source case management platform for small OSINT teams. Lookup results are held as proposals that a person must accept before entering the case graph, with export regenerated from the graph. Pre-1.0.
strengths: Human-in-the-loop acceptance of machine results supports defensible provenance
Clear architecture and stack documentation with CI and coverage badges
risks: Pre-1.0 with schemas and API shapes changing without notice
Not hardened for multi-tenant or production deployment

workspace-analysis.description: Terminal-first local OSINT field workbench with rigorous evidence provenance. Cases, content-addressed evidence, origin clustering, contradiction candidates, honest tool catalogue. Local-first, no telemetry.
workspace-analysis.summary: A terminal-first local OSINT workbench that stores collected evidence as hash-addressed copies under scoped cases, tracks claims and relations with analyst review, clusters origins, flags contradictions, and exports integrity-checkable bundles.
strengths: Content-addressed evidence verifiable with sha256sum
Clear limitations and status tracking
Local-first with no telemetry
risks: Alpha pre-release with small username provider set
TUI experimental
Catalogue entries lack adapters yet

workspace-analysis.description: Offline desktop workspace for organizing OSINT investigations.
workspace-analysis.summary: OpenTrace is an offline Windows/Linux desktop app (PySide6) for organizing OSINT investigations with a visual board, tasks, sources, hypotheses, journal, SHA-256 integrity info, and portable case folders. No telemetry or accounts.
strengths: Fully offline with no telemetry or accounts
Visual investigation board with relationships and exports
Tests in CI on Windows and Ubuntu
risks: Early-stage project with limited documentation of data formats
Binary release targets Windows x64 only

workspace-analysis.description: Open source alternative of Palantir Gotham  🌟 Star if you like it! 🌟'
workspace-analysis.summary: Open-source intelligence integration and link-analysis platform meant as an alternative to Palantir Gotham, with ontology-driven data fusion, graph visualization, GIS mapping, timelines and an AI co-pilot. Much of the described functionality is planned rather than implemented.
strengths: Clear purpose as a Gotham-style analysis workspace
Backend and frontend setup steps given
risks: Heavy marketing language with little concrete detail on data sources
Many features listed as planned rather than working
Defense and law enforcement targeting without stated legal safeguards
